question_1: What should I do if my set-top box won't turn on?
question_4: no lights on the set-top box
question_5: I press the power button but nothing happens
answer: Check that the power adapter is firmly connected to both the mains socket and the back of the set-top box. If you're using a power strip, check its power switch, then unplug the power cable and reconnect it after 10 seconds. If the power indicator still doesn't light up, the unit will need to be checked by our support team.

question_1: What should I do if my set-top box keeps restarting?
question_2: the box keeps turning off and on
question_5: the power comes on and immediately goes off again
answer: Check the power cable and adapter connections, and make sure there is enough ventilation around the set-top box. If it is overheating, switch it off and let it cool for 5 minutes before turning it back on. If the same problem persists, the power adapter or device may need to be inspected.

question_1: What should I do if the power light is on but the TV screen is blank?
question_2: the power is on but no picture
question_3: the box light is on but the TV is black
question_4: it seems to have booted but there's no picture
question_5: the power is fine but no input signal
answer: Make sure the TV's external input is set to the HDMI port where the set-top box is connected. Unplug and replug the HDMI cable, then restart both the TV and the set-top box. If the screen is still blank, try a different HDMI port or cable.

question_1: What should I do when the TV displays 'No Input Signal'?
question_4: the TV says there's no signal
answer: Press the external input button on the TV remote and select the HDMI input where the set-top box is connected. Check that the HDMI cable is not loose, then switch the set-top box off and back on. If you have multiple HDMI ports, try a different one.

question_1: What should I do if the picture freezes or breaks up?
answer: Restart the set-top box and router in sequence. Unplug the router, wait 10 seconds, plug it back in, and once your internet connection is restored, restart the set-top box. If the problem only occurs on a specific channel or app, it may be a service outage.

question_1: What should I do if the screen is black but I can hear audio?
question_2: there's sound but the screen is black
question_4: I can hear the audio but there's no picture
question_5: the screen looks as if it's turned off
answer: Check the HDMI cable connection and the TV's external input setting. The set-top box resolution may be set to a value the TV doesn't support — restart the set-top box and reset the display settings to default. If the problem continues, try a different HDMI cable.

question_1: What should I do if the picture doesn't fit the TV screen?
question_2: the picture is being cut off
answer: Check the aspect ratio or resolution setting in the set-top box menu. Also check the TV's picture size, overscan, and native picture mode settings. If the picture is still cropped after making changes, restart both devices.

question_1: What should I do if UHD or 4K picture quality is not showing?
answer: Check whether your TV and HDMI cable support UHD or 4K. In the set-top box display settings, set the resolution to Auto or 4K and connect to a 4K-compatible HDMI port. Note that if the content itself doesn't support UHD, it will play in standard quality.

question_1: What should I do if my set-top box won't connect to Wi-Fi?
question_4: the Wi-Fi password isn't being accepted
question_5: I can't connect to the router
answer: Check that Wi-Fi is enabled in the set-top box settings, then re-enter the router name and password. If the router is too far away, move closer and try again. If it still fails, restart the router and attempt to reconnect.

question_1: What should I do if the internet connection keeps dropping?
question_3: the connection drops while I'm watching
answer: Restart the router and set-top box, and where possible connect via a wired ethernet cable to check stability. If using Wi-Fi, reduce obstructions between the router and set-top box, and choose the more stable band between 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz.

question_1: What should I do if a wired LAN connection isn't working?
question_5: the LAN cable is plugged in but there's no connection
answer: Make sure the ethernet cable is firmly plugged into both the router and the set-top box. Try a different port or replace the cable. If the problem persists after restarting the router, the broadband line or equipment may need to be checked.

question_1: What should I do if an app opens but video won't play?
question_2: the app opens but video won't load
question_4: YouTube opens but videos won't start
answer: First check your internet connection, then restart the set-top box and router. If the problem is limited to one app, close it fully and reopen it, and check for any available updates. If playback fails across multiple apps, a network outage is likely.

question_1: What should I do if video keeps buffering?
answer: Check whether multiple devices are using the internet at the same time. If using Wi-Fi, move the set-top box closer to the router or connect via ethernet. If buffering only occurs with high-definition content, try lowering the quality as a temporary fix.

question_1: What should I do if the remote control buttons aren't working?
question_3: I press buttons but nothing happens
question_5: I can't control it with the remote
answer: Replace the remote control batteries with new ones and check that the set-top box is switched on. Remove any objects blocking the IR receiver on the front of the set-top box. If it's a Bluetooth remote, it may need to be paired again.

question_1: What should I do if remote control pairing fails?
answer: Place the remote close to the set-top box and press the pairing button combination again. If the connection has become confused, restart the set-top box and try pairing again. Low battery charge can also cause pairing to fail, so try new batteries.

question_1: What should I do if the remote control won't turn on the TV?
question_2: the remote won't switch the TV on
question_3: the TV power button does nothing
question_4: the integrated power control isn't working
question_5: the set-top remote won't turn on the TV
answer: The remote may be set to control only the set-top box power. Check the TV power control or universal remote settings in the set-top box menu. Note that the integrated power function may not be supported by all TV makes and models.

question_1: What should I do if the voice button on the remote isn't working?
question_4: speaking into the remote does nothing
answer: Check the microphone permissions or voice service settings. Some models require the remote to be connected via Bluetooth for the voice button to work. Try pairing the remote again, then restart the set-top box and try once more.

question_1: What should I do if I've lost the remote control?
question_4: I've lost it and can't control the box
answer: Check whether the set-top box or mobile app supports a remote finder feature. If not, you can temporarily use a mobile remote app, and contact our support team to purchase or replace the remote.

question_1: What should I do if there's no sound from the set-top box?
answer: Check that neither the TV nor the set-top box is muted, and turn up the volume. Reconnect the HDMI cable and reset the set-top box audio output settings to default. If you're using a soundbar, also check its input mode.

question_1: What should I do if the audio and picture are out of sync?
question_5: the sound lags behind the picture
answer: Check the audio delay correction settings on the TV or soundbar. Try switching the set-top box audio output to Auto or PCM. If you're using a soundbar, switch to the TV speakers to see whether the delay improves.

question_1: What should I do if there's no sound in one particular app?
question_2: there's no sound only in Netflix
question_4: only one app has no audio
question_5: there's no sound inside the app
answer: Check the mute or volume settings within the app, then close the app fully and reopen it. If sound is working normally in other apps or live TV, the issue is likely with that specific app. Try updating the app or restarting the set-top box.

question_1: What should I do if there's no sound from the soundbar?
question_3: the soundbar is connected but silent
question_4: there's no sound on the ARC connection
question_5: no audio from the speaker bar
answer: Check that the soundbar is switched on and set to the correct input mode for the connection type (HDMI ARC, optical, or Bluetooth). Reconnect the cable and check the TV's audio output settings.

question_1: What should I do if the Netflix app won't open?
answer: Check the internet connection on the set-top box and close then reopen the Netflix app. If the problem persists, restart the set-top box and check for app updates. Login or payment issues must be resolved separately through your Netflix account.

question_1: What should I do if the YouTube app freezes or closes unexpectedly?
answer: Close the YouTube app fully and reopen it, then restart the set-top box. If the internet connection is unstable, video may freeze, so check your Wi-Fi or LAN. If the problem recurs, try clearing the app cache or updating the app.

question_1: What should I do if I can't log in to an app?
question_4: the password is correct but login fails
answer: Double-check your username and password, and verify that the same account works on a mobile phone or PC. If the date and time on the set-top box are incorrect, it may cause login failures. Account lock or payment issues must be resolved through the app's support team.

question_1: What should I do if an app won't install or update?
question_5: nothing will download from the store
answer: Check the storage space and internet connection on the set-top box. If storage is low, delete unused apps or clear the cache, then try again. If updates keep failing, restart the set-top box and try once more.

question_1: How do I update the set-top box software?
question_2: where do I update the software?
question_3: how do I do a system update?
question_4: how do I update the firmware?
answer: Go to Device Information or System Update in the set-top box settings. Do not switch off the box or unplug any cables during the update. The set-top box may restart automatically once the update is complete.

question_1: What should I do if the set-top box is slow after an update?
question_4: it's responding slowly since the update
answer: It's normal for the box to be temporarily slow immediately after an update while apps are being optimised. Wait about 5 minutes, then restart the set-top box. If it remains slow, check storage space and remove any unused apps.

question_1: What should I do if I've forgotten my password?
question_4: I don't know my login password
question_5: I'd like to recover my account password
answer: Passwords cannot be retrieved directly from the set-top box. Use the forgotten password option in the relevant service, or recover your account from a mobile phone or PC. For data protection reasons, agents are unable to provide your password directly.

question_1: What should I do if the problem isn't resolved after trying the self-help steps?
question_2: I've tried everything and it still doesn't work
answer: If you've already unplugged the power, checked the HDMI, and restarted the router and set-top box but the problem continues, the device or broadband line may need to be inspected. Note down any error codes shown on screen and contact our support team.
